correctness.rationale: Reconstructed RESULT.md (1)–(5) directly. The facet means give vertex coefficients (a−p_i)/d summing to zero. Affine independence realizes any prescribed vertex values; a 0/1 assignment across the signs gives the total-variation formula. If all weights are uniform, the ratio is zero in every direction. Outward-normal equilibrium and nonparallel facet normals imply 0<p_i<1/2. For h weights above a, dG=∑_{heavy}p_i−ha; h=1 gives dG<1/2−a, h≥2 gives dG<1−ha, and h=0 gives zero. This proves strictness. For the flattened coordinate simplex, the opposite-zero facet's Gram matrix is a rank-one update of a diagonal matrix, giving area sqrt(1+(d−1)t²)/(d−1)!; the other areas are t/(d−1)! or 1/(d−1)!. The weights tend to (1/2,0,…,0,1/2), proving sharpness. In d≥3 the deficit <a excludes h=0,1 and h≥3, so the remaining mass equals the deficit exactly. Normal equilibrium bounds the dominant weighted sum by η, and their two deficits from 1/2 sum to η, yielding 4η after the triangle inequality. The supplied finite checker was inspected, not run; the decisive steps are analytic.

value.rationale: This solves the motivated sharp convex-body centroid problem within the basic class of simplices and yields a computable shape-specific invariant, not just another bound. The precise deficit-to-area identity and nearly opposite normals explain the geometry of the sharp degeneration and are useful beyond the scalar constant. The elementary signed-weight representation alone would be routine; the exact sharp subclass and inverse conclusions are the substantive package.
